title: Closed-loop advocate preemptions (recurrence flag) + one-off citation-parity sweep for hardcoded-monitoring WINs
problem: ISS-3025 (from curmudgeon WIN-045.c5) raised two pipeline-design questions. (a) ISS-2861-style dashboard-anchor citation patches are discovered one-at-a-time when a curmudgeon cycle happens to notice asymmetry between sibling WINs; c5's angle-2 defense (rated 2/5) was exactly this procedural asymmetry being usable as rhetorical ammunition. Ad-hoc audit this run: 36 WINs are in the hardcoded-monitoring scope, 7 fail parity today (WIN-004/009/016/017/029 lack any dome-artifact citation (raw-text/NN-*.txt, monitor.py, claim_index.json, status_history.json); WIN-010/019 carry 'appear(s) to be' hedges despite having citations). (b) advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation entries silently age out: WIN-045.c4 (2026-05-05, defense_survives=3) recommended a specific Newtonian-forcing sentence; nothing tracked whether it landed; WIN-045.c5 (2026-07-27, 83 days / 1 full cycle later) found the same defense still unpreempted at the same 3/5 rating. digest-reviews.js already SURFACES preemptive_recommendation per-review (truncated 300 chars), and decider-curmudgeon.md already creates defense EXPs at defense_survives>=3 -- but nothing detects RECURRENCE, so a dropped/consolidated recommendation (WIN-045's went into the EXP-499->EXP-514 consolidation and the specific sentence never landed) re-enters the pipeline at base priority as if new, or not at all.

proposed_fix.summary: Part B (the structural fix): make recurrence mechanically loud. digest-reviews.js computes recurrent_defense_cycles -- the count of consecutive PRIOR review cycles for the same item whose advocate_mode.defense_survives was also >=3. decider-curmudgeon.md escalates any recurrent defense one priority level, requires quoting the prior cycle's preemptive_recommendation verbatim in the EXP notes, and requires grep-verification that the preemptive text actually landed in data/wins.json before issue closure. Part A (the bounded cleanup): a one-off audit script monitor/scripts/audit-citation-parity.js sweeps all hardcoded-monitoring WINs for citation parity (dome-artifact citation present, no hedge phrases); decider runs it once and batches patches for the 7 currently-flagged WINs; NOT a scheduled agent -- after the one-off sweep, Part B's recurrence escalation plus normal curmudgeon coverage is the regression detector. Rationale for not scheduling: population is bounded (36), the quiet period makes daily checks pure cost, and adding a 15th scheduled surface for a solved one-time asymmetry is the over-engineering direction the pipeline has been pruning since the 2026-06-23 quiet-period cadence cuts.

files_to_create.purpose: One-off (re-runnable) citation-parity audit for hardcoded-monitoring WINs. RC=0 clean, RC=3 flagged (house canary convention). Registration checklist per ISS-3000/3001/3011/3019: classify as git-owned source code -- add to workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH; no FUSE round-trip.

files_to_modify.explanation: Helper added immediately above run(); uses existing loadJSON/REVIEWS_DIR/path. Skipped cycles (missing file) intentionally break the count -- consecutive-cycle recurrence is the signal, not lifetime total.
Digest entry field addition; baseId and review are in scope in the digest loop.

files_to_modify.replace:
2. Create open issue with `category: "defense"`.
3. Priority: rating 3→moderate, 4→major, 5→critical.
4. **Recurrence escalation (PROP-149 / ISS-3025b).** If the digest entry carries `recurrent_defense_cycles >= 1`, this same defense already survived at least one full prior review cycle without its preemptive recommendation landing in text (canonical case: WIN-045 c4's Newtonian-forcing sentence sat unintegrated 83 days until c5 re-found it). Do three things: (a) bump priority ONE level above the rating baseline (3→major, 4→critical, 5 stays critical); (b) quote the PRIOR cycle's `advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation` verbatim in the EXP notes so consolidation cannot silently drop the concrete sentence again; (c) at integration time, before closing the issue, verify the preemptive text actually landed by grepping `data/wins.json` for a distinctive phrase from the recommendation — if the grep is empty, the EXP is NOT integrated regardless of what the tracker status says. Never re-file a recurrent defense at base priority.
files_to_modify.explanation: Makes recurrence escalation + landed-text verification an explicit decider obligation, closing the silent-age-out loop.

registration_checklist: audit-citation-parity.js: add to workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH (git-owned source code); it is NOT a per-run integrity artifact so no FUSE_EXCLUDE_TRANSIENT entry needed; no build.js OWNERSHIP entry needed (never crosses to FUSE as data). digest-reviews.js + decider-curmudgeon.md are already classified git-owned.
tradeoffs: GAIN: silent-age-out class structurally eliminated (recurrence is loud at intake, escalated, and closure requires text-grep proof); the 7-WIN parity debt gets cleared in one decider batch instead of ~7 future curmudgeon-cycle discoveries (~1 per cycle at current cadence); no new scheduled agent, no new data surface, no new ownership classification beyond one NEVER_PUSH line. LOSE/RISK: (1) recurrent_defense_cycles adds a per-digest-entry disk walk of prior-cycle files -- bounded by cycle count (<=8 observed), negligible; (2) the hedge-phrase heuristic in Part A has false-positive potential ('appears to be' can be legitimate in non-verdict prose) -- mitigated because output routes through decider judgment, not auto-patch; (3) priority-bump on recurrence could over-escalate if a defense is genuinely unresolvable-by-design (curmudgeon keeps rating it 3 forever) -- mitigated: decider can file wontfix with reasoning, which stops the EXP re-creation loop; (4) grep-verification at closure adds one manual step per defense EXP -- that step is exactly the missing control the 83-day case proves is needed.
estimated_impact: Prevents multi-month rhetorical-vulnerability windows (the review's public credibility surface); saves an estimated 1-2 curmudgeon cycles per affected WIN that currently get spent re-discovering unintegrated recommendations; Part A closes a 7-WIN consistency debt the dome author could otherwise cite as process asymmetry (c5 angle-2).
why_human_needed: build-scripts/digest-reviews.js is build infrastructure (needs a build cycle + operator apply per Mode 4 self-fix exclusions); the recurrence-escalation policy changes decider triage behavior, which is a workflow-design decision ISS-3025 explicitly asked to have considered rather than unilaterally applied; new-script registration touches workspace-sync.md (NEVER_PUSH edit is operator-applied by convention).
verification_pattern: grep -q 'recurrent_defense_cycles' build-scripts/digest-reviews.js && grep -q 'Recurrence escalation' monitor/prompts/reference/decider-curmudgeon.md && test -f monitor/scripts/audit-citation-parity.js && echo FIXED || echo STILL_BROKEN
